main_text.p: tre, secundum Paulum ? innuens locum ad Hebraeos C. vii.3.

XXIII. Isidorus Pelusiota, Chrysostomi discipulus, clarus temporibus Concilij Ephesini, sub Theodosio juniore, Libro 1. Epistolarum, Epist. xciv. in locum Hebr iv. 13. Τὰ γυμνὰ καὶ πεπραχηλισμένα τῷ πολυφρονι γεγραπται Παύλῳ ut scriptum est sapientissimo Paulo. Libro ii. Epist. Lviii [?] citaturus locum Hebr.1,3. de Christo effulgentia gloriae &c. charactere Personae Patris, Ταῦτα ἐννοήσας ὁ θεσπέσιος Παῦλος, καὶ ὥσπερ ἐνθὺς γενόμενος, Haec animadvertens divinus ille Paulus, & quasi numine afflatus &c. Sic alibi passim.

XXIV. Cyrillus, Episcopus Alexandrinus, Praefes Concilij Ephesini; Epistolam ad Hebraeos utique Paulo transcribit; ita Thesauro de sancta Trinit. λόγῳ [?], citat locum Hebr.ix.24. his verbis, ὁ Παῦλος ἐπιστέλλων, φησίν, Paulus in Epistola scribens dicit; sic locum adducturus Hebr. i.1,2,3. Παῦλος Ἐβραίοις διαλεγόμενος, καὶ μετὰ πολλῆς παρρησίας, &c. Paulus ad Hebraeos differens, & multa quidem cum

page.notes: Greek passages are copied from a small, heavily inked scan; the Greek words in the Isidorus entry and the Cyrillus line "λόγῳ" are uncertain and should be checked against the original. "Lviii" in the Isidorus entry is doubtful. The page is a single text column with no marginal notes. The fragment "tre," at the top is the end of a word from the previous page, with its first letters lost. The printed text ends mid-sentence with "cum", which is also the catchword.
